key_insight: A genome-guided, physics-informed screening framework can cut a huge double-perovskite search space down to a few DFT-validated, phase-stable, lead-free absorber candidates.
engineering_relevance: This provides interpretable design rules for accelerating discovery of non-toxic semiconductors for photovoltaics, sensors, and transparent electronics.
method: Trained ML surrogates on 1,221 DFT-calculated A2BB'X6 compounds using four descriptor families: packing, bonding, polarization, and electronic identity.
Used a staged inverse-design filter on 13,088 charge-balanced compositions to enforce stability and target optoelectronic performance.
Validated top candidates with DFT and assessed thermodynamic and optical properties.
evidence_signal: The stability classifier reached ROC-AUC 0.92 and the band-gap regressor achieved R2 = 0.93 on held-out data, with five final candidates on the convex hull (Ehull <= 0 meV/atom).
watch_item: The workflow depends on DFT-labeled training data and compositional constraints, so experimental synthesis and defects/disorder effects still need validation.
paper_title: Genome-Guided Interpretable Screening of Phase-Stable, Lead-Free Double Perovskite Absorbers for All-Inorganic Semiconductors, Sensors, and Photovoltaics with DFT-Validated Design Rules
